_notes: The living cast of a parish: the handful of named parishioners who keep turning up. Roles are tags on the generated people (cast:<role>); the lines are templated with {Name} (how the parish says it), {first}, {he}/{his}/{him}. The year moves them: deaths, moves, marriages, births, and a new face in a vacated role. Numbers in systems/cast.ts are invented.

sacristan.label: the sacristan
lines: {Name} has the sacristy keys on a ring the size of a saucer and will not have a second set cut.
{Name} laid out the wrong colour for the feast and was right, as it turned out; the ordo had a footnote.
{Name} found the third candle-lighter in the flower cupboard and has said nothing about it, loudly.
{Name} was in the sacristy at six for the seven o'clock, as {he} is every day, and had the cruets filled before you were dressed.
{Name} has opinions about the way the lectors close the book and shared one of them.
{Name} polished the thurible on Saturday and it is not to be used on Sunday, apparently.

flowers.label: the flowers
lines: {Name} did the flowers for the weekend and there were lilies, which was a decision.
{Name} has a quarrel with the florist on the avenue that predates you and will outlast you.
{Name} left the altar bare for Lent with the air of someone who has been asked not to.
{Name} brought the flowers from {his} own garden this week, and the church smelled of it.
{Name} asked whether the bishop would be coming, on account of the flowers, and was told no, and did the flowers anyway.

usher.label: an usher
lines: {Name} ushered the ten-thirty and moved a family of six into the front pew with a hand on the father's elbow.
{Name} counted the house at every Mass and wrote the numbers on the back of a bulletin, which is the only attendance record the parish keeps.
{Name} found a wallet in the fourth pew and had it returned before the owner knew it was gone.
{Name} stood at the back with {his} arms folded through the homily, which is how {he} listens.
{Name} has a word for latecomers and used it on a man who turned out to be the new deacon's father.

choir.label: the choir
lines: {Name} sang the psalm and held the last note longer than the organist wanted.
{Name} has been in the choir since a pastor nobody else remembers and knows every descant by heart.
{Name} asked whether the choir might do the Latin at Christmas, and looked at the organist while asking.
{Name} was hoarse this week and sang anyway, from the back row, so as not to be heard.
{Name} brought a new alto to practice, {his} niece, who can read music, which changes things.

counter.label: counts the collection
lines: {Name} counted the collection on Monday with the same two people as always and the same coffee.
{Name} noticed a fifty in the basket folded into a square and wondered aloud whose it was.
{Name} has kept the count in the same ledger for years and does not trust the envelope company.
{Name} was late to the counting and the other two waited, because they will not open the bag without {him}.
{Name} asked, carefully, whether the second collection had been announced, because the numbers said not.

youth.label: one of the young people
lines: {first} served the seven o'clock and got the bells right for once.
{first} asked after Mass what a priest does all week, and listened to the answer.
{first} has a friend who might come to the youth group, if there were one, and said so.
{first} was at the back with a phone and put it away when you looked, which is progress.
{first} is thinking about the seminary, or a friend of {his} is, or {he} wanted to see what you would say.

widow.label: a widow of the parish
lines: {Name} was at daily Mass every morning this week, in the same pew, with the same rosary.
{Name} brought a cake to the rectory door and would not come in.
{Name} asked you to remember her husband at the Mass on Thursday, which you did.
{Name} has the Sunday paper delivered to the rectory now, for reasons {he} will not explain.
{Name} told you a thing about the pastor before last that you will not repeat.

arguer.label: has opinions
lines: {Name} stopped you on the steps about the homily, again, and was not entirely wrong.
{Name} has written to the bishop before and mentioned it in a tone that meant {he} would again.
{Name} asked why the Mass was in Spanish at eleven and did not want the answer.
{Name} thinks the parish council should meet in public and said so at the parish council.
{Name} disagreed with the bulletin, in the bulletin, in a letter the secretary printed out of spite.

family.label: one of the family
lines: The {last}s took up the whole of the fifth pew on Sunday, three generations, and the youngest slept through it.
{Name} asked if the family could have the hall for a baptism party and did not ask what it cost.
{Name} brought the whole family to the fish fry and they stayed to wash up.
{Name} mentioned that the {last}s have been in the parish since it was a mission, which is true and which everyone knows.
The {last}s were not at Mass this week, all of them, which means a wedding somewhere or a quarrel.

died: {Name} died on {day}. The funeral was on the Saturday, and the church was fuller than it is on Sunday.
{Name} died at home, in {his} sleep, and the family found the parish bulletin folded on the bedside table.
{Name} died after a short illness. You had anointed {him} the week before, and {he} knew what it was for.
moved: {Name} moved away to be near a daughter, and came to the rectory to say so, and cried at the door.
{Name} has moved to the other side of the city and will drive back for Sunday, {he} says, which will last until winter.
{Name} sold the house and went south. The parish will not replace {him}; it will just close over the gap.
married: {first} was married on Saturday, in this church, and asked you to do it.
{first} married a girl from the parish across the river, and the two parishes argued about which church.
{first} was married and the {last}s filled a side of the church.
born: {Name} had a baby, a {child}, and brought {him2} to the ten-thirty at nine days old.
A {child} for the {last}s. The baptism will be in a month, and the hall is already spoken for.
{Name} has a new {child}, and the older children have opinions about the name.
arrived: {Name} has started doing what {who} did, without being asked, and nobody has said no.
{Name} moved into the parish in the spring and by summer was {role}, which is how it goes.
{Name}, who nobody had noticed for a year, has quietly taken over as {role}.
farewell: The last Sunday. {names} stood at the back after Mass and did not leave until you did.
The last Sunday. There was a cake in the hall, and {names} made speeches nobody had asked for.
The last Sunday. {names} shook your hand at the door, and one of them did not let go.
